primitives.name: Odds Transitivity
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Odds transitivity**: from π_i/π_j × π_j/π_k = π_i/π_k consistency conditions, derive the logistic pairwise form.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\pi_i': 'positive worth parameter for competitor i (dimensionless)', 'P(i \\text{ beats } j)': 'probability that i defeats j (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Pairwise odds must satisfy transitivity: if i beats j and j beats k, then i beats k.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Intransitive outcome structures where odds cycles occur.

layer2.mapping: Transitivity implies a consistent ordinal ranking structure compatible with logistic utility functions.
layer2.telemetry: Win matrix intransitivity index (e.g., cycle detection in directed graph).

primitives.name: Luce Choice Axiom
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Luce choice axiom**: pairwise choice probabilities consistent with a global "worth" scale imply BT.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\pi_i': 'worth parameter for item i (dimensionless)', 'S': 'set of available items (finite subset of competitors)', 'P(i \\text{ chosen from } S)': 'probability of selecting i from S (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Choice probabilities are invariant under irrelevant alternatives and proportional to item worths.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When choices violate independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA).

layer2.mapping: Luce’s axiom leads to the same pairwise probability structure as Bradley–Terry under additive utility.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation from IIA in multinomial choice data.

primitives.name: Maximum Entropy Retrodictive Criterion
primitives.verbatim_quote: **MaxEnt/ML under retrodictive criterion**: BT as the maximum-entropy distribution constrained by sufficient statistics (wins per item).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w_i': 'number of wins for competitor i (integer)', '\\pi_i': 'worth parameter for competitor i (dimensionless)', 'P(\\text{outcome})': 'likelihood of observed results (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Given observed win counts, the most uncertain distribution consistent with them is the BT model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sufficient statistics do not fully characterize outcome variability.

layer2.mapping: Entropy maximization under win-count constraints yields the BT likelihood function.
layer2.telemetry: KL divergence between fitted BT and empirical frequency distributions.

The Bradley–Terry model arises from several distinct yet equivalent mathematical motivations. From odds transitivity, consistency of pairwise comparisons implies a logistic form. The Luce choice axiom shows that if choices follow a global worth scale, they must be BT-compatible. Maximum entropy principles show that BT is the least informative distribution given win counts. Hazard models suggest BT emerges from first-arrival times in continuous-time races. Spectral methods connect BT to centrality measures in networks. Each path reveals a different facet of the model’s universality. However, BT fails when transitivity breaks down, ties are common, or multi-competitor dynamics dominate. These failure modes inform model selection criteria in GSE’s adaptive pipeline.
